description: Implements FORMULATION.md section 4 in full: normalizes all nine features, imputes missing ones at the cohort median, applies the locked weights, clips to [0,1]. Returns both the score and a per-feature contribution frame for UI explainability.
signature: def compute_complexity_score(frame: pd.DataFrame, tags: pd.DataFrame, params: EnrichmentParams) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.DataFrame]
docstring:
Compute complexity_score for every candidate.

Args:
    frame: normalize_features' output, indexed by appid, plus compute_developer_catalog_size's Series merged in as a 'dev_title_count' column.
    tags: The run's extracted tag rows (appid, tag, votes, rank).
    params: EnrichmentParams -- weights, complexity_bounds, simplicity_tags, complexity_tags.

Returns:
    (complexity_score, contributions): complexity_score is a pd.Series in [0,1] (or NaN, see below) indexed like frame. contributions is a DataFrame, one column per feature in FORMULATION.md section 4's table, holding each feature's weighted contribution (w_f * n_f(x)) for that row, so the UI can render a per-game breakdown (reporting.CaseStudy.complexity_drivers).

Steps per feature:
    1. Compute the raw feature value column (install size -> size_bytes; early-access duration -> early_access_days, 0 when is_early_access is False; dev catalog size -> dev_title_count; simplicity/complexity tag scores -> compute_tag_score; achievement/DLC/language counts -> the corresponding raw columns; platform count -> linear normalize over {1,2,3} as (platform_count-1)/2).
    2. Normalize: log-scaled features via normalize_feature_log_scaled(x, a, b) using params.complexity_bounds[feature]; if that feature's bounds are absent (pre-freeze) or degenerate, skip step 2's log transform for that feature and treat every row's raw normalized value as NaN, deferring entirely to imputation in step 3 -- consistent with ADR-012's 'earlier runs' derived scores are provisional until this script has been run once'. The negative-weighted simplicity_tag_score feature is inverted (1 - score) before weighting, so that a HIGH simplicity-tag match contributes a LOW complexity value, matching FORMULATION.md's 'Normalizer: linear, negative' description.
    3. Impute: impute_missing_at_median for each feature's normalized column across the candidate cohort.
    4. Weight and sum: complexity_score = clip(sum(w_f * n_f), 0, 1).
    5. If more than a configured share of a row's features were imputed AND raw-missing (not just pre-freeze-unnormalizable) simultaneously (see enrichment module's own edge case 'More than a configured share of a row's complexity features missing -> complexity_score NULL'), that row's complexity_score is set to NaN instead of a computed value.

Imputed features per row are recorded (via the was_imputed flags from impute_missing_at_median, OR'd into a single per-row imputed_features_json list) for enrichment.EnrichmentReport.imputation_rate_by_feature and games_enriched.imputed_features_json.
preconditions: frame has a dev_title_count column already merged from compute_developer_catalog_size
postconditions: Every non-NaN complexity_score value is in [0, 1]
complexity_score is NaN exactly for rows meeting the too-much-missing-data threshold, never for an ordinary single-feature imputation

contributions' columns sum to complexity_score for every non-NaN row (before the final clip; a clipped row's contributions may sum to slightly outside [0,1], which is expected and documented, not a bug)

edge_cases.input: A row with every complexity feature present and within its normalization bounds
edge_cases.expected_behavior: no imputation; complexity_score computed directly from the weighted sum

edge_cases.input: All rows in the run missing early_access_days (e.g. no early-access titles survived the coarse filter at all)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: impute_missing_at_median raises ValueError internally for that feature (all-NaN column); compute_complexity_score catches it and falls back to the documented 0.5 midpoint for every row's early_access_days contribution, emitting a run-level warning event

every log-scaled feature is entirely imputed at the cohort median (since none can be normalized), which for a fresh run 1 means every row gets an identical median contribution for those six features -- complexity_score is therefore driven almost entirely by the three non-log-scaled features (simplicity/complexity tag scores, platform count) until run 1 completes and freeze_empirical_parameters.py fixes the bounds; this is a known, intentional degradation, not a bug, and must be surfaced to the user as a caveat on run 1's results specifically

edge_cases.input: A row with 6 of 9 features missing (above the too-much-missing threshold)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: complexity_score is NaN; row is excluded from apply_simplicity_filter's buildable subset but retained for density counting, per the module's own edge case

edge_cases.input: complexity_score computed sum is 1.15 before clipping (possible if all normalized features happen to sit near 1 while weights sum to exactly 1 -- should mathematically not exceed 1 if every n_f <= 1 and weights sum to 1, but floating-point drift is guarded)

unit_tests.name: test_weighted_sum_matches_hand_computation
unit_tests.description: A synthetic row with known normalized features and the locked weights reproduces the exact hand-computed weighted sum, per the module's own testing requirement.
unit_tests.expected: matches hand-computed value to floating-point tolerance

unit_tests.name: test_clipping_holds_at_extremes
unit_tests.description: An all-minimum-feature row scores 0; an all-maximum-feature row scores 1.

unit_tests.name: test_median_imputation_applied_and_flagged_never_zero
unit_tests.description: A row missing achievement_count gets that feature's contribution at the cohort median, not 0, and imputed_features_json lists 'achievement_count'.

unit_tests.name: test_too_much_missing_data_yields_null_score
unit_tests.description: A row missing 6 of 9 features yields complexity_score == NaN.

unit_tests.name: test_empty_complexity_bounds_pre_freeze_falls_back_to_median_for_all_log_features
unit_tests.description: With params.complexity_bounds == {}, every log-scaled feature is imputed at the cohort median rather than normalized.
unit_tests.expected: log-scaled feature contributions identical across all rows (all at the cohort median)

unit_tests.name: test_all_rows_missing_one_feature_falls_back_to_midpoint
unit_tests.description: A feature that is NaN for every row in the cohort falls back to the documented 0.5 midpoint rather than raising out of compute_complexity_score.
unit_tests.expected: that feature's contribution == 0.5 * w_f for every row
